title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Grothendieck sets up the arithmetic of Weil q-numbers in a CM field. These are the possible Frobenius eigenvalues of motives, or abelian varieties, over F_q.

Setting: K is a totally real number field, L ⊃ K a totally imaginary quadratic extension (a CM field), and q = p^r. One looks for λ (in L; the 'K' on the page is a slip) with λ·λ̄ = q^i, i.e. |λ| = q^{i/2} in every complex embedding, for suitable i. Such λ are automatically p-units, i.e. units away from p. They form a subgroup W of L^×, now allowing i ∈ Z.

Structure step: write λ = q^{i/2}·u with u a p-unit satisfying u·ū = 1. The set of such u is a group U. Consider the valuation map U → Z^P, u ↦ (v_𝔓(u))_{𝔓∈P}, where P is the set of primes of L above p.
- Kernel: the units u with uū = 1 have absolute value 1 at all archimedean places, so they are roots of unity (Kronecker). The kernel is therefore finite.
- Image: since uū = 1, one has v_𝔓(u) = −v_{𝔓̄}(u). Hence a prime of K above p that is inert or ramified in L contributes 0. The image lies in a lattice Z^{Q'}, one coordinate per prime of K above p that splits in L. It has finite index there, by Dirichlet's S-unit theorem: if 𝔓^h = (α) (h from finiteness of the class number), then α/ᾱ hits h·e_𝔓.
- Conclusion: in the case where every prime of K above p splits in L, U/μ(L) ≅ Z^Q, with Q the set of primes of K above p.

This is exactly the computation of the character group of the Weil-number torus (the protorus P_q, or the kernel of the motivic Galois group of motives over F_q). It is also the arithmetic input for Honda–Tate. It fits the dossier 'Théorie de Galois des motifs': determining the motivic Galois group of the category of motives over F_q, assuming the standard and Tate conjectures.

The neighbouring pages are an unrelated typescript (Steinberg, 'Regular elements of semisimple algebraic groups') filed in the same folder.
errors: λ should lie in L (the CM field), not K. For λ ∈ K totally real, λλ̄ = λ² and the question degenerates.
The decomposition λ = q^{i/2}u requires q^{i/2} ∈ L. This fails for odd i·r unless √p ∈ L. Strictly one gets λ^2 = q^i u^2 or must work up to finite index / in L(√p).

'U ≅ Z^Q' holds only modulo the finite torsion subgroup μ(L), and the image of U in Z^Q is only of finite index (abstractly free of rank |Q|). In general the rank is the number of primes of K above p that split in L, not |P|.

ideas.what: Group of Weil q-numbers in a CM field and its structure via p-adic valuations: finite kernel (roots of unity) and image of finite index in Z^{split primes of K above p}
ideas.modern_name: Weil-number group / character group of the Weil-number torus P (Langlands–Rapoport 'pseudomotivic' group); motivic Galois group of Mot(F_q)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Honda (1968) and Tate (1968–71) for Weil numbers versus abelian varieties; Langlands–Rapoport (1987) and Milne (1994, 'Motives over finite fields') for the Weil-number protorus as the motivic Galois group; Saavedra Rivano (1972) partially
ideas.where_published: unsure; the idea that motives over F_q are governed by Frobenius/Weil numbers appears in Grothendieck–Serre correspondence and is reported in Saavedra's thesis

ideas.what: Units of a CM field with uū=1 are roots of unity; rank of p-units of relative norm 1 equals number of primes of K above p splitting in L
ideas.modern_name: Dirichlet S-unit theorem for CM fields (relative unit/S-unit rank)

missed.claim: Within the 1965 dossier on the Galois theory of motives, Grothendieck explicitly computes the structure of the group of Weil q-numbers in a CM field. That group is the character group of the torus later identified (Langlands–Rapoport 1987, Milne 1994) as the motivic Galois group of motives over F_q. This documents that he had the 'Weil-number torus' computation in hand early, possibly before Honda–Tate. The dating of the page, between 1965 and about 1977, is uncertain.
missed.quote: On cherche les λ ... tels que λλ̄ = q^i ... Ces u forment un groupe U, et l'hom U → Z^P u ↦ (v_𝔓(u)) ... U ≃ Z^Q
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a priority/historical point for the motivic Galois group over finite fields and the Langlands–Rapoport torus. The mathematics itself is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The computation is standard today, being the character group of the Weil-number torus. What is of some historical interest is seeing it worked out by Grothendieck in his notes on motivic Galois theory, plausibly predating Langlands–Rapoport and Milne. The page is fragmentary, the date is uncertain, and there is no new result.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'Soit K une extension tot. réelle finie de Q' – the crossed-out word is 'de'; fine.
'les λ ∈ K' – the handwriting reads K, but mathematically it must be L.
'pour i convenable ∈ N' is an interlinear insertion after |λ| = q^{i/2}; the following line reads roughly 'ce sont des unités exc. p, et'.
'unités absolues exc. p' (underlined, crossed out) refers to absolute units / Weil numbers.
'D'après le th. de Dirichlet' plausibly reads 'D'après le th. des unités'; the target is something like 'Z^{(P)'}' and the image is 'd'indice fini'.
Marginal note at left near line 'reel. ...' reads approximately 'vel. iK)' – unclear.
'splitté en deux dans L' is underlined.
